newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to get tough with nuisance neighbours.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to get tough with nuisance neighbours.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party declared war on noisy and disruptive neighbours on Tuesday, pledging to enlist nuisance squads and even private detectives to crack down on trouble-makers if it won power.

Courts would be given powers to restrain anti-social behaviour by curfews and exclusion orders as well as curbs on making noise and issuing threats under proposals unveiled by Jack Straw, the main opposition party's home affairs spokesman.
Breaches of Labour's planned new Community Safety Order (CSO) would be punishable by up to four years in prison.
"Anti-social behaviour in neighbourhoods is undermining far too many communities. Many thousands of people are suffering from harassment and intimidation," Straw told a news conference.

Noise pollution is a growing problem in Britain. A total of 144,943 people complained about barking dogs, loud music, do-it-yourself maintenance and other domestic noise in 1995, compared to 131,153 in 1994.

The Conservative government recently introduced regulations giving local health officers powers to confiscate noise-making equipment from Thursday. From April 1997 they will be able to apply new maximum noise limits in the hours of darkness.
The next election is due by May 1997 and Labour are around 20 points ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls.
Straw said Labour's CSO would give police and local authorities the powers they needed to provide relief for thousands whose lives were being made hell in their own homes.

"The present legal arrangements are not up to the task. The criminal law fails to deal with what can be sustained "low level' harassment and intimidation, while the injunction procedure is slow, cumbersome and generally only applicable to council tenants," Straw said.
The private detectives would be used to gather evidence on serious anti-social behaviour, for example in cases where local witnesses might be too afraid to testify for fear of reprisal.
